blocks.text: (used with verbs) behind, beyond — за- + -йти́ (“to go”) → зайти́ (“to go behind, to go beyond; to call on”)

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch

blocks.text: за- — an action after which the object ends up behind some boundary, real or imagined

«действия над предметом, объектом, в результате которого последний оказывается за какой-либо воображаемой или материальной линией» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of за-. Its examples: забить, забросить, забрести.

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: to drive in (nail), to hammer in, to nail up; to score (a goal)
to throw, to cast, to hurl (somewhere); to send
(colloquial) to stray, to wander; (colloquial) to drop in

blocks.text: за- — covering, or being covered, with something
«покрыть или покрыться, прикрыть или прикрыться чем-либо» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of за-. Its examples: забрызгать, замазать, запотеть, запудрить, заржаветь.

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: to paint over; to stick with putty

blocks.text: (with verbs) onto, upon — на- + идти́ (“to go”) → найти́ (“to find”)

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: to find; (figuratively) to think, to consider
